DEFINITION
Human development is the scientific study of processes of change & stability.
Process of growing to maturity.  
Study of a human life-cycle from conception to death.
In biological terms, this entails growth from a one-celled zygote to an adult human being.

GROWTH
Growth is quantitative
Growth comprises of height, weight, size & shape of body organs
Cell  division
Growth is for limited period

DEVELOPMENT
Development is qualitative as well as quantitative 
In this with physical changes, cognitive, social & emotional change also included
Due to motor development & adjust mental processes & their interplay
Development takes place till death
 It can be observed by matured behavior

Growth & Development
Growth
Implies  physical change, usually resulting from either an increase in cell number or cell size
Development:
A change or modification in a person’s capacity to function; enhancement of a skill

BALTES’s LIFE SPAN DEVELOPMENT
Paul B. Baltes & Colleagues Identified Six Key Principles of Life Span Development
Development is life long
Development involve both gain & loss
Relative influence of biology & culture shift over  life span
Development involves a changing allocation of resources
Development is modifiable
Development is influenced by historical and cultural context

CHILD DEVELOPMENT
INTRODUCTION 
Child development is  multifaceted, integral, & continual process of change in which children become able to handle ever more complex levels of moving, thinking, feeling, & relating to others.

Cont..
Child development is a gradual unfolding of biologically determined characteristics & traits that arises as child learns from experiences 
The first 1000 days of life span from day of conception till  child attends two years of age (UNICEF), is consider most important development phase.


https://www.unicef.org/laos/ensuring-healthy-start-first-1000-days-0

Cont…
Globally, more than 200 million children under five years fail to reach their potential in cognitive & social development due to poverty, poor health, malnutrition & deficit care
Most of which is borne by developing countries
Most of these children live in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, are exposed to multiple risks including poverty, malnutrition, poor health & un-stimulating home environment, while detrimentally affecting their development.

Cont…
Other factors that compromise overall development during pregnancy & after birth are parent’s behavioral, dietary deficiencies, chronic infections, exclusive breastfeeding, inadequate feeding practices & lack of stimulation
Over 43% of children under the age of 5 are at risk of not fulfilling their full developmental potential as per   UNICEF in 2017

CHILD DEVELOPMENT
Child development refers to  biological & psychological changes that occur in human beings between birth & end of adolescence
Individual  progresses from dependency to increasing autonomy
Gradual  change  occurs as  central nervous system matures & shows psychological reactions

Cont…

At birth , brain has 100 billion neurons

Number of synapses remain constant but number of neurons decreases gradually
Used pathways - preserved , & less used ones atrophy

The development of child takes place in stages. Each stage has certain unique characteristics & in each stage, certain types of behavior or traits are more conspicuous than others. 
Entire period of development is divided into following stages
PRENATAL-PERIOD- It is mainly physiological and consists of growth of all body parts.

Cont..
INFANCY-  A period of newborn. Growth is temporarily at a standstill. 
 BABYHOOD- At this stage, the babies are completely helpless during the early part. Gradually they learn to control the muscles so that they can become independent.
CHILDHOOD- This period lasts from two to thirteen years of age. It is subdivided into two parts: 
EARLY CHILDHOOD- The child learns to gain control over the environment and starts learning to make social adjustments.
LATE CHILDHOOD- It is the period when sexual maturity occurs and adolescence begins. The major development is socialization.

Cont..
ADOLESCENCE- It is twelve years onwards till the individual assumes adulthood. It is again divided into two stages: 
EARLY ADOLESCENCE- Physical growth is rapid in both boys and girls. There is enhanced mental activity in general.
LATER ADOLECENCE- it is characterized by tapering off of physical growth but the psychological development continues in many complex ways preparing him to adjust to the demands of society as an adult. 
ADULTHOOD- By this time, physical changes are nearly complete but the psychological adjustments continue throughout the entire stage.

Cont…
OVERVIEW OF DEVELOPMENTAL PERIODS:
Prenatal period: from conception to birth
Infancy & toddlerhood: birth to 2 years
Early childhood: 2-6 years old
Middle childhood: 6-12 years old
Adolescence: 12-19 years old

Cont…

MOTOR SKILLS DEVELOPMENT

MOTOR MILESTONES
Motor skills - actions that involve movement of muscles in body
Divided  into two groups: 
Gross  motor skills
Fine motor skills 
Motor skills typically develop together since many activities depend on  coordination of gross & fine motor skills 

  https://hands.fiu.edu/2019%20-%20Gonzalez,%20Alvarez,%20Nelson%20-%20Front%20Psychol%20-%20Systematic%20Review.pdf

GROSS MOTOR MILESTONES
Milestones acquisition occurs  in  cephalocaudal sequence
In Orderly & sequential manner but rate of achievement may vary
Generalized activity is replaced by specific individual responses
Certain primitive reflexes have to be lost to gain voluntary control

Cont..
Gross motor skills are  abilities required in order to control  large muscles of  body
Skills for use to move  whole body, arms & legs
Include sitting, crawling, walking & balance, running, jumping 
Development  of these skills begins when  child is in  womb & continues throughout life

Cont..
       0-1 MONTH
Prone – pelvis high, knees drawn up under abdomen, lifts off chin partly
Supine – lies with flexed posture
Pulled to sit– complete head lag
Held in sitting position– back uniformly rounded
Held standing – flops at hips & knees

Cont..
    2 MONTHS
Prone – pelvis high, hips partly extended, lifts off chin to some extent
Supine – lies with flexed posture
Pulled to sit– partial head lag
Held in sitting position– back uniformly rounded, can hold head momentarily
Held standing – flops at hips & knees

Cont..
   3 MONTHS
Prone – lifts off chin with head at 45⁰, supports on forearms
Supine – lies with flexed posture, head to the side
Pulled to sit– less head lag
Held in sitting position– less rounding of back, head held up occasionally bobbing to side
Held standing – holds head

Cont..
    4 MONTHS
Prone – pelvis flat, holds chin & shoulder off couch for long, weight borne on forearms
Supine – symmetric posture


Pulled to sit– head steady
Held in sitting position– back straighter, head held well
Held standing – pushes down with feet

Cont..
    5-6 MONTHS
Prone – holds chest & upper abdomen off couch for long, weight borne on hands
Supine – puts feet in mouth
Rolls from prone to supine
Held in sitting position– back straighter, sits with support
Held standing – bears full weight on legs

FINE MOTOR DEVELOPMENT
All fine motor activities are built upon four important skills
These skills ought to be learned before  child accomplish complicated tasks
Grasping objects
Reaching out to objects
Releasing objects deliberately
Turning  wrist in various directions

1 MONTH
Vision – fixes gaze, regard objects when brought into line of vision 3 feet from eyes
Motor – tightly clenched hands

2 MONTHS
Vision – follows a moving person past midline

Motor – no more clenched hands

3 MONTHS
Vision – hand regard, follows dangling object from side to side (180 degrees)

4 MONTHS
Vision – follows objects more efficiently

COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
Mental  action or process of acquiring knowledge & understanding via thought, experience & senses
Focuses on mental processes of perceiving, remembering, believing & reasoning 
Reasoning- essence of intelligence-Piaget studied in order to discover “how we come to know” (Singer & Revenson, 1997) 
Cognitive development (Piaget), cumulative- understanding  new experience grows out of  previous learning experience

Cont..
   Cognitive Development 
Developmental theory views cognition as  sequential & increasingly complex unfolding of biologically driven abilities , influenced by  environment 
Five  basic aspects of development - language, visual-motor tasks, fine motor development, gross motor development, & social behavior

Cont..

At varying ages, children sequentially attain abilities that become increasing complex 
Mediated  by two central features;  
Increasing development of "working memory“ & influence of "expertise"  
Children develop at varying rate

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
Sensorimotor stage (Infancy)
In this period (6 stages) intelligence  demonstrated through motor activity
During this stage senses, reflexes, & motor abilities develop rapidly
Intelligence  displayed as reflex movements become more refined 
Acquire object permanence

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
Pre-operational stage (Toddler & Early Childhood)
In this period (two sub-stages) intelligence  demonstrated through use of symbols, language use matures, memory & imagination developed, yet thinking  in  non logical, non- reversible manner
Egocentric thinking predominates

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
Pre-operational stage 
Begins  to take greater interest in objects & people around, from only one - own point of view
Stage of curiosity-questioning & investigating new things-limited experience
Children ’s thought differs  most from adult thoughts

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
Concrete operational stage (Elementary & early adolescence)
Characterized by 7 types of conservation: number, length, liquid, mass, weight, area, volume
Intelligence  demonstrated through logical & systematic manipulation of symbols related to concrete objects
Operational thinking develops
Egocentric thought diminishes

Cont..
Concrete Operational Stage
Begins  when child  able to perform mental operations
Child  can count from 1-10, but  actual understanding that one stands for one object only appears in  stage of concrete operations
Primary  characteristic - Reversibility

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT.
Formal operational stage (Adolescence & adulthood)
Intelligence demonstrated through  logical use of symbols related to abstract concepts
Early in  period - return to egocentric thought
Only 35% of high school graduates in industrialized countries obtain formal operations - many people do not think formally during adulthood

STAGES OF COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT
 
Individual can conceive all  possible ways to solve  problem & approach  problem from numerous points of view 
Thought more flexible, rational & systematic
Adolescent  can think about thoughts & “operate on operations not just concrete objects
Can  think about  abstract concepts as space & time
Develops inner value system & sense of moral judgment
Has  necessary “mental tools” for living  life

Social / Adaptive Development

Social / Adaptive Development 
Social development is related to  Social, Emotional & Personal development of an individual
Infant begins taking in information through  senses, she/he must begin  process of interpreting & giving meaning to that information - called Perceptual development

Cont…
Earliest  pattern or object for focus of interest, & instrumental in learning in an infant’s life is  human face
Before an infant can  comprehend language or  environment,  begins to understand  meaning of certain expressions on  primary caregiver's face
Visual social cues signal  infant information about  perceiving world, whether joy, fear, apprehension, or another human emotion that is being expressed by  caregiver

Cont…
Refers  to  range of behaviors  child acquires during  developmental process to function independently
Sub-domains comprise of Self Care, Community Self-sufficiency, Personal-social Responsibility  & Social Adjustment
Advance  delineation results in  form of dressing/undressing, eating/feeding, toileting  & grooming, appropriate behavior in different settings, adjusting to new situations, & attending appropriately

Cont…
Adaptive behaviors are learned & involve ability to adapt to & manage one's surroundings to effectively function & meet social or community expectations.
Good adaptive behavior promotes independence.
Socially unacceptable behaviors that interfere with  acquisition of desired skills & performance  of everyday activities are classified as maladaptive behaviors.
Maladaptive behavior interferes with child's achievement of independence as child requires more supervision & assistance in order to learn appropriate behavior.

Cont…
Social  aspect of  development relates specifically to  interaction of people, dependent on  different social situations that the individual is subjected to
In contrast,  emotional side of  development relates to understanding & ability to control one’s emotions, which again is dependent on  situation
Both  emotional   &  social  development relate specifically to internal & external progression of individual

Cont…
Both  social & emotional concept of development is measured during a child’s growth which is split up into different stages
At each stage  child should be demonstrating a different aspect of social development  
Older  the child, more progressed this social development should appear

Cont…
In  terms of social development , growth is evaluated based on the different behavioral  characteristics
These behaviors will reflect child’s growth & level of understanding while progressing into adulthood  
Good social development imperative, as progression determine their social skills - allowing them to display proper reactions to specific social/emotional situations

Cont....

New-born help adults succeed as caregivers by being Readable , Predictable & Responsive
Social referencing- searching for cues to help interpret situation from care-givers or communicating  partners
Infants  generally use parent’s expressions as signals to guide their interpretations & reactions to various  events & situations
